# A positive forced-site owner can create an unbounded second return debit

22 October 2026. This extends the
[first return-debit family](SECONDARY_TEN_SHARP_RETURN_DEBIT.md).
The new conclusion is uniform in two independent, unbounded parameters.
Consuming the next forced support can create a debit proportional to
the width of an earlier occupied band, even when the new owner has
positive charge. Thus two forced-owner steps, endpoint
disjointness and positive-owner counting alone cannot establish a
nonnegative selected-union compensation rule.

The construction is a partial family of complete original U records.
It does not assert a complete feasible extension and does not refute
the global inequality or the selected-pair theorem. Its enlarged
family still has a forced support requiring another owner.

## Two independent even parameters

Let h>=12 and g>=4 be even. Construct H3 with two blocks,

    a_0=31, s_0=0, w_0=h, w_1=12,
    z_0=z_1=g+24, root breadth6.

Then a_1=g+49,s_1=-24. Add

    R=U(32,10,g+2), chart(g+38+r,2-c),
    T=U(6,4,g), chart(g+41+r,-23-c),
    W=U(2g+20,4,40), chart(2g+42-c,r-34).

R and T have selected-pair gain4. W consumes their common forced
support x=(2g+41,-30), has marginal-3 and leaves z=(22,7) forced.
The first-return proof remains valid for any h: only the first six
columns of the P_0 bar participate, and every earlier base endpoint
remains to the right of R. In particular

    Phi(H3+R+T+W)-Phi(H3)=1.

Now add the positive original

    V=U(6,4,h+8), chart(r,c)=(16+c,h+15-r).          (1)

It consumes z as its far terminal and is endpoint-disjoint from ALL
the previous records. Its exact marginal and combined gain are

    DeltaPhi(V | H3+R+T+W) = -h/2-2,
    Phi(H3+R+T+W+V)-Phi(H3) = -h/2-1.             (2)

Both formulas hold for every permitted h,g. The second quantity tends
to minus infinity with h, even with g fixed or with both earlier far
legs arbitrarily long.

## Endpoint geometry and source charge

V's two-column bar occupies columns h+14,h+15 and rows17,...,22.
Its near leg is row17, columns h+11,...,h+15. Its far leg is row22,
columns7,...,h+15. All H3 endpoints are at rows at least23. The
earliest old endpoints are the P_0 bar at row23, columns1,...,h+12.
R and T start below row22. W's bar is left of column-32, its short
leg lies at row2g+41, and its far leg is row22, ending at column6.
This proves endpoint disjointness and z in V without a size cutoff.

Direct immutable-source counts for V are

    matching=h/2+11,
    endpointTiles=h/2+10,
    originalSupportsInside=h/2+10,
    charge(V)=1.

The bar has four endpoint tiles, the near leg adds two and the far
leg adds (h+8)/2. Both bar-end supports and both axial terminal supports
lie inside. The near leg contributes two lateral supports at intrinsic
even rows2,4; the far leg contributes (h+8)/2 at intrinsic even rows.
Thus the inside count is4+2+(h+8)/2=h/2+10. V therefore adds
one positive-owner count and no negative mass. This is precisely why
positive-owner count by itself cannot pay the following event debit.

## Exact new full tiles and directed events

Physical tiles are specified by even top-left coordinates. Every NEW
mixed full tile is in the band at rows22,23. Their top-left corners are

    (22,c), c=6,8,...,h+10.                         (3)

There are h/2+3. At c=6 the upper-left belongs to W, upper-right to V,
and both lower cells to P_0. All other tiles have V above and P_0 below.
The c=6 tile was not full before V and is counted once. V's remaining
bar tiles are single-owner tiles, which are not mixed full tiles.

The complete NEW directed-event list is

    P_0:(23,c) -> V:(22,c), c=7,...,h+12;
    V:(22,c) -> P_0:(23,c), c=8,10,...,h+12.        (4)

The first row contributes h+6 events and the second h/2+3, for
3h/2+9 altogether. The downward directions from odd V columns are
excluded by V's immutable original lateral supports. The two horizontal
W/V directions between (22,6) and z are excluded by their respective
axial supports. The P_0 upward event at column6 already existed before
V; it is not counted a second time. There are no other foreign endpoints
in V's physical endpoint tiles. Consequently (3) and (4) give

    1+2(h/2+3)-(3h/2+9) = -h/2-2,

proving (2) for all parameters. No old mass, old positive-owner count
or earlier full-tile credit has been reused.

## The next forced support and the precise obstruction

The point q=(23,h+13) is an original lateral support of V and an
original bar-end support of P_0. It is absent from the enlarged
endpoint union. Its occupied endpoint neighbours are exactly

    V:(22,h+13), P_0:(23,h+12).

Its other two neighbours are absent. Thus every complete extension
containing this partial family must consume q with another fresh
original. That next original cannot be a rotor. Indeed its internal
endpoint neighbours at q must lie south or east. A rotor endpoint
having this restriction is a terminal. Substitution in the eight
rotor symmetries gives four distinct relative endpoint patterns:

| Pattern | Own neighbour at q | A mandatory extra relative endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| South terminal, first chirality | (1,0) | (2,1) |
| South terminal, second chirality | (1,0) | (2,1) |
| East terminal, first chirality | (0,1) | (-1,1) |
| East terminal, second chirality | (0,1) | (2,1) |

But q+(2,1)=(25,h+14) is an endpoint of the retained root K, and
q+(-1,1)=(22,h+14) is an endpoint of V. Every possible rotor
therefore collides with a retained endpoint. This is an exhaustive
fixed-shape substitution, uniform in h,g, not a bounded search over
unclassified U dimensions. Under the full U/rotor model, q must be
consumed by another U. Complete extendibility remains open.

The counterexample is to a rule on partial selected unions: neither
two successive forced-site receptions nor requiring the second owner
to have positive charge guarantees nonnegative new compensation.
Any proof valid for actual complete families must either exclude
these returns by complete-closure constraints or account jointly for
the next q-consumer and the old band without reusing an earlier
reserve. The target global inequality has not failed.

The exact-set verifier checks every new full tile and owner-labelled
event, both source-count increments, the variable-width first return,
the next forced support, all four rotor exclusions and invariance
under even translations. The
scoped Lean module proves the conditional receipt arithmetic and
unboundedness. Neither replaces the written source-chart proof.
This later result is outside the both-far main-theorem review input.

# A forced-site consumer can return a three-unit debit to the first block

22 October 2026. This follows the
[sharp both-far family](SECONDARY_TEN_BOTH_FAR_SHARPNESS.md).
It gives a general, explicitly verifiable obstruction to inferring a
nonnegative new-owner increment merely from endpoint disjointness and
occupation of a forced support. It does NOT refute the selected-pair
theorem, assert a complete extension, or refute the global target.

## An all-even-parameter family

For any even g>=4 use the sharp construction with m=1,a_0=31,s_0=0:
two old blocks, w_0=w_1=12,z_0=z_1=g+24,root breadth6. Thus

    a_1=g+49, s_1=-24,
    R=U(32,10,g+2), chart(g+38+r,2-c),
    T=U(6,4,g), chart(g+41+r,-23-c).

Let H=H3 union {R,T}. The sharp theorem gives DeltaPhi(H|H3)=4.
Its missing common support is

    x=(2g+41,-30),

with north endpoint in R and east endpoint in T. Consider the FULL U

    W=U(2g+20,4,40), chart(r,c)=(2g+42-c,r-34).       (1)

It contains x as its short-leg terminal, with internal neighbour west.
Its original endpoints are disjoint from ALL of H. Its original charge
is -1. The exact increments are

    DeltaMass=1, DeltaMixedFull=3, DeltaEvents=10,
    DeltaPhi(W|H)=1+2*3-10=-3,
    DeltaPhi(H union {W}|H3)=1.                      (2)

This holds for every even g>=4, with both earlier far legs unbounded.
The new width 2g+20 is essential to the family: a bounded-width search
can miss this return even when it samples large g.

## Endpoint geometry and charge

W's bar is the aligned two-column strip {-34,-33} at rows22,...,2g+41.
Its short leg is row2g+41, columns-34,...,-30, ending at x. Its far
leg is row22, columns-34,...,6. Both legs are contiguous, and the
complete original supports and matching are retained.

All old endpoints have column at least-28, so W's bar and the
nonterminal part of its short leg lie to their left. The selected
R/T far columns are-30,-29; R ends immediately above x and T is
immediately east. Hence W's short leg has no endpoint collision with
H. The far leg lies at row22. The earliest old endpoints are P_0's
bar at row23, while all other old originals begin farther down; the
selected R/T also begin below row22. Thus the entire W is endpoint-
disjoint from H for every g.

The matching count is 2g+41. Its endpoint footprint has g+10 bar
tiles,2short-leg tiles and20far-leg tiles, hence g+32 tiles. Exactly
22original support points lie in that footprint: one per leg tile,
including the terminal axial supports. Its charge is consequently

    (2g+41)+22-2(g+32)=-1.

## Exact new physical sets

At x the new mixed full tile has top-left (2g+40,-30): its upper-left
cell belongs to R, both right cells to T, and lower-left to W.
The ONLY new event in that tile is

    W:x -> R:(2g+40,-30).

W's east target is its original axial support, T's west target is
T's original support, and R's south target is R's original axial
support, so all three of those directions remain excluded. Old R/T
horizontal events at the upper row already existed and are not counted
again. The local site therefore supplies one full tile and one event.

The return far leg lies immediately above P_0's old bar:

    P_0=U(24,10,4), chart(23+r,25-c).

Its bar at row23 occupies columns1,...,24. The new mixed full tiles
have top-left (22,2) and (22,4). The exact surviving directed events are

    P_0:(23,c) -> W:(22,c), c=1,...,6;
    W:(22,c) -> P_0:(23,c), c=2,4,6.

At odd columns W's downward target is an original lateral support.
At physical columns{0,1}, P_0 has no endpoint at column0, so that
tile is not full. At columns{6,7}, W ends at6 and its axial support7
is not an endpoint, so that tile is also not full. There are exactly
two full tiles and nine events in this return region, signed value-5.

W's aligned bar consists of single-owner full tiles and creates no
mixed tile/event. Its remaining short-leg tile has no foreign endpoint.
The displayed local and return regions are physically disjoint, and
all old event/support exclusions are immutable. Adding mass one,
local signed value+1 and return signed value-5 proves (2), without
an enumeration or length cutoff.

## Closure is transferred, not finished

The point z=(22,7) is W's original far axial support. It is absent
from H union W, but has endpoint neighbours W:(22,6) and P_0:(23,7).
It must therefore be consumed by another new original in every complete
extension containing this partial family. The other two endpoint
neighbours are absent. This gives a concrete return to the first block,
not a support-closed negative family.

What fails is the inference

    endpoint-disjoint new original consuming the forced site
    implies a nonnegative Phi increment.

The four-unit selected-pair theorem remains true for its stated selected
union. Whether the family including W admits a complete feasible extension
is OPEN, so this is not a counterexample about actual complete families
or the global inequality. A successful next compensation argument must
include the new z-consumer and its return receipt, not just the number
of forced owners or the local tile at x.

The exact-set verifier retains all original source records, checks all
three new full tiles and all ten owner-labelled events, the charge
counts, both increments, and the next missing support. Finite controls
supplement the all-g proof. No separate Lean or independent review of
this later obstruction is claimed; it lies outside review780b9242's input.

A subsequent [second-return theorem](SECONDARY_TEN_UNBOUNDED_SECOND_RETURN.md)
allows arbitrary first-block width h>=12. A positive owner consumes z
but has marginal-h/2-2, giving total selected increment-h/2-1 and
leaving the next support q=(23,h+13) forced. Complete extendibility
remains open; this stronger partial-family obstruction does not refute
the global inequality.

# Exact source charges and separation of earlier originals

22 October 2026. This addresses the REVISE verdict in audit780b9242
of the both-far selected-pair theorem. Its geometric assessment supports
the gain identity, nonstacking, triple-owner correction and automatic
pair-footprint separation. Its proposed charge correction is false
for the supplied original-source constructor. The proof-text objection
about earlier blocks is valid and has been repaired in the E-frontier
note. No independent acceptance is inferred from this response.

## Direct source counts

For R=U(L,10,f) at chart(a-11+r,C+1-c), a and C are odd and all
dimensions even. Its first bar row and leftmost endpoint column are
even. The full two-row bar therefore consists of L/2 physical tiles.
Each leg contributes depth/2 further endpoint tiles, giving

    matching = L+4+f/2,
    endpointTiles = L/2+5+f/2.

The original supports at intrinsic coordinates (0,0) and (0,L+1)
have absolute columns C+1 and C-L. These are respectively in the
next tile to the right and the previous tile to the left of the bar.
Neither far stem nor near stem occupies their tile columns. They are
therefore outside the ENTIRE endpoint tile footprint, not just the bar.
At depth10 the four odd lateral rows3,5,7,9 lie in endpoint tiles;
at depth f the f/2-1 odd lateral rows3,...,f-1 do likewise. Both
axial terminal supports lie in the terminal endpoint tile. Thus

    originalSupportsInside = 4+(f/2-1)+2 = 5+f/2,
    charge(R) = (L+4+f/2)+(5+f/2)-2(L/2+5+f/2) = -1.

For T=U(M,4,g) at chart(a-8+r,s+1-c), the offset is odd/odd.
Its corresponding counts are

    matching = M+1+g/2,
    endpointTiles = M+2+g/2,
    originalSupportsInside = 4+g/2,
    charge(T) = 1-M.

The bar occupies M/2+1 physical tile columns and two physical tile
rows; its leg additions give the displayed endpoint-tile count.
Both original bar-end supports are now inside. The near and far
lateral supports contribute1 and g/2-1, and both axial supports
are inside. Hence the inside count is2+1+(g/2-1)+2=4+g/2.

Both charges are negative. One pair contributes negative mass
1+(M-1)=M and no positive-owner count. The exact selected-pair
Phi identity is unchanged. These counts use immutable original supports,
regardless of which other owners later occupy their locations.

In the audit's concrete triple-owner example, R=U(54,10,26) at
offset(38,2) has matching71, endpointTiles45, insideSupports18:
charge71+18-90=-1. The claimed inside count20 includes the two
outside bar-end supports. T=U(28,4,24) at offset(41,-23) has
matching41, endpointTiles42, insideSupports16 and charge-27.
The pair mass is28, exactly as asserted by the original verifier.
The sharp E witness U(50,10,22) has counts65,41,16 and charge-1.

## Uniform separation from every earlier original

Use the H3 notation and even dimensions of the both-far theorem.
At internal index i, C_i=s_i+w_i+13=s_(i-1)+1 is odd. Partition
the earlier records into the nine base originals B_j, added repair
P_j, west rotor Z_j, south U X_j and the root K.

For every j<i, all B_j endpoints have column at least s_j+2,
including their unbounded long stem. Since offsets decrease, this
is at least s_(i-1)+2=C_i+1. All R endpoints have column at most
C_i. Odd C_i and even C_i+1 lie in different physical tile columns,
so there is no common endpoint tile, mixed full tile or intratile event.
The root has minimum column s_0+w_0+14>=C_i+1 and is separated
by the same argument for arbitrary root breadth.

Earlier P_j,Z_j,X_j may occupy columns at or left of C_i. Their
maximum rows are respectively a_j+2,a_j-1,a_j+2. Since each
anchor gap is at least18, every such endpoint has row at most
a_i-16. R's minimum endpoint row is the even number a_i-11.
Their physical tile rows are therefore strictly smaller than those
of R. This exhausts all earlier originals without any far-leg cutoff.

For R's far strip, the simpler minimum-column bound s_j-4 still
applies. The distinctions above repair the overbroad claim that all
earlier blocks lie to the right. Own-block and first-later-frontier
receipts retain their original proofs and exact sets.

The companion verifier checks the closed-form counts, the exclusion of
both R bar-end supports and inclusion of both T bar-end supports,
and every earlier-owner separation in nonuniform chains. These finite
checks supplement the all-dimension proof. Scoped Lean establishes the
conditional count algebra and the integer physical-row/column bounds;
the source-set counts and chart exhaustion are written arguments.

"""Exact all-original sets for a width-dependent positive-owner return debit."""

import itertools
import json

from check_cooperative_promotion import neighbors
from check_demand_hull_reserve_obstruction import independent_source
from check_incident_eight_north_transfer import charge, shift
from check_secondary_ten_arbitrary_t_consumers import old_chain
from check_secondary_ten_both_far_charge_separation import counts
from check_secondary_ten_both_far_compensation import originals
from check_secondary_ten_internal_consumer_chains import phi_from
from check_secondary_ten_north_contact_debit import inventory
from rotor_networks import rotor, transform_module


if not __debug__:
    raise RuntimeError('Run without -O: verification uses assertions.')


def main():
    cases = []
    for width, far, translation in itertools.product(
            (12, 14, 50, 2000), (4, 6, 40, 2000), ((0, 0), (-64, -100), (20, 200))):
        fixed, unused, unused, sites = old_chain(31, 0, [width, 12], [far+24]*2, 6)
        receiver, consumer = originals(sites, [width, 12], (1, 6, 0, far+2, far))
        first = independent_source((2*far+20, 4, 40),
                                   (True, False, True), (2*far+42, -34))
        second = independent_source((6, 4, width+8),
                                    (True, True, False), (16, width+15))
        fixed = [shift(record, translation) for record in fixed]
        receiver, consumer, first, second = [shift(record, translation)
                                            for record in (receiver, consumer, first, second)]
        moved = lambda point: (point[0]+translation[0], point[1]+translation[1])
        paired = fixed+[receiver, consumer]
        base = paired+[first]
        old, pair_receipt, before, after = [inventory(records)
                                           for records in (fixed, paired, base, base+[second])]
        assert phi_from(paired, pair_receipt)-phi_from(fixed, old) == 4
        assert phi_from(base, before)-phi_from(paired, pair_receipt) == -3
        assert counts(second) == (width//2+11, width//2+10, width//2+10)
        assert charge(second) == 1
        assert after['mass'] == before['mass']
        assert sum(charge(record) > 0 for record in base+[second]) == 1+sum(
            charge(record) > 0 for record in base)
        full = {(moved((22, column))[0]//2, moved((22, column))[1]//2)
                for column in range(6, width+12, 2)}
        events = {(19, moved((23, column)), moved((22, column)))
                  for column in range(7, width+13)}
        events |= {(len(base), moved((22, column)), moved((23, column)))
                   for column in range(8, width+13, 2)}
        assert after['full']-before['full'] == full and len(full) == width//2+3
        assert after['events']-before['events'] == events and len(events) == 3*width//2+9
        assert before['full'] <= after['full'] and before['events'] <= after['events']
        assert phi_from(base+[second], after)-phi_from(base, before) == -width//2-2
        assert phi_from(base+[second], after)-phi_from(fixed, old) == -width//2-1
        occupied = set.union(*(record[0] for record in base+[second]))
        support = moved((23, width+13))
        assert moved((22, 7)) in first[1] & second[0]
        assert support in second[1] & fixed[19][1] and support not in occupied
        assert set(neighbors(support)) & occupied == {
            moved((22, width+13)), moved((23, width+12))}
        witnesses = {moved((25, width+14)), moved((22, width+14))}
        assert moved((25, width+14)) in fixed[18][0]
        assert moved((22, width+14)) in second[0]
        patterns = set()
        for symmetry in itertools.product((False, True), repeat=3):
            module = transform_module(rotor(), symmetry)
            record = module['endpoints'], module['selected'], {
                tuple(sorted(edge)) for edge in module['matching']}
            for anchor in record[0]:
                internal = {(point[0]-anchor[0], point[1]-anchor[1])
                            for point in set(neighbors(anchor)) & record[0]}
                if not internal or not internal <= {(1, 0), (0, 1)}:
                    continue
                candidate = shift(record, (support[0]-anchor[0], support[1]-anchor[1]))
                assert candidate[0] & witnesses
                patterns.add(frozenset(candidate[0]))
        assert len(patterns) == 4
        cases.append(dict(width=width, far=far, translation=translation,
                          second_marginal=-width//2-2, total_selected_increment=-width//2-1))
    print(json.dumps(dict(status='PASS', exact_original_set_controls=len(cases), cases=cases,
        rotor_exclusion_controls=4*len(cases),
        scope='General written two-parameter unbounded positive-owner return debit. '
              'Exact NEW full/event sets, next forced support and rotor exclusion checked. Complete '
              'extendibility OPEN; no global inequality or selected-pair counterexample.'), indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

CONSTRUCTOR check_incident_eight_north_transfer.charge

def charge(record):
    tiles = {(row//2, column//2) for row, column in record[0]}
    selected_inside = {point for point in record[1] if (point[0]//2, point[1]//2) in tiles}
    return len(record[2])+len(selected_inside)-2*len(tiles)


CONSTRUCTOR check_secondary_ten_north_contact_debit.inventory
RESOLVED_CALLS {"charge": "check_incident_eight_north_transfer.charge", "neighbors": "check_cooperative_promotion.neighbors"}
def inventory(records):
    endpoints = set.union(*(record[0] for record in records))
    assert len(endpoints) == sum(len(record[0]) for record in records)
    tiles = {(row//2, column//2) for row, column in endpoints}
    full = set()
    for tile in tiles:
        cells = {(2*tile[0]+row, 2*tile[1]+column)
                 for row, column in itertools.product(range(2), repeat=2)}
        if cells <= endpoints and not any(cells <= record[0] for record in records):
            full.add(tile)
    events = {(index, point, target) for index, record in enumerate(records)
              for point in record[0]
              for target in (set(neighbors(point)) & endpoints)-record[0]-record[1]
              if (point[0]//2, point[1]//2) == (target[0]//2, target[1]//2)}
    mass = sum(max(0, -charge(record)) for record in records)
    return dict(mass=mass, full=full, events=events,
                raw_reserve=mass+2*len(full)-len(events))

CONSTRUCTOR check_demand_hull_reserve_obstruction.independent_source
RESOLVED_CALLS {"affine": "rotor_networks.affine"}
def independent_source(parameters, symmetry, offset):
    width, left, right = parameters
    matching = [((0, column), (0, column+1)) for column in range(1, width, 2)]
    matching += [((1, column), (1, column+1)) for column in range(2, width-1, 2)]
    matching += [((row, column), (row+1, column))
                 for column, height in ((1, left), (width, right)) for row in range(1, height, 2)]
    support = {(0, 0), (0, width+1), (left+1, 1), (right+1, width)}
    support |= {(row, 0 if row % 2 == 0 else 2) for row in range(2, left+1)}
    support |= {(row, width+1 if row % 2 == 0 else width-1) for row in range(2, right+1)}
    move = lambda point: affine(point, symmetry, offset)
    return ({move(point) for edge in matching for point in edge},
            {move(point) for point in support},
            {tuple(sorted((move(first), move(second)))) for first, second in matching})


CONSTRUCTOR rotor_networks.affine
RESOLVED_CALLS {}
def affine(point, symmetry, offset=(0, 0)):
    transpose, flip_row, flip_column = symmetry
    row, column = point
    row = -row if flip_row else row
    column = -column if flip_column else column
    if transpose:
